name: Shadow Mountain Free Dispersed Primitive Camping Area - Bridger-Teton NF

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Jackson Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 5 consecutive days max stay limit within Teton Basin area
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted only at designated designated campsites along Forest Service Road 30340. Must park within designated site post markers.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in granitic soil, 200 feet from streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Grizzly Bear territory: IGBC-approved bear canister or hard-sided vehicle food storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in designated stone/metal fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch with water.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Stage 1 and Stage 2 fire restrictions enforced in late summer.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and gravel mountain forest road (FS 30340 / Shadow Mountain Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard dirt road with steep grades, ruts, and deep dust. Slow speeds required.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance car or CUV/SUV recommended (Normal low clearance 2WD cars can reach lower site turnouts in dry weather, but high clearance required for upper mountain sites)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 4-5 bars 5G/LTE (30-90 Mbps download speeds overlooking Jackson Hole valley)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Direct line of sight across Jackson Hole valley to Grand Teton towers)

amenities: Jaw-Dropping Unobstructed Views of Grand Teton (13,775 ft)

services_available: Grand Teton National Park Visitor Center

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: Late May thaw: cold (35-50°F), high snowmelt mud, road opening around late May.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Ideal Rocky Mountain summer (75-85°F daytime, crisp 40-45°F nights), dry sunny skies, afternoon lightning storms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular aspen leaf color in September (50-65°F daytime, freezing 20-30°F nights), prime boondocking.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe sub-zero mountain winter (-15 to 20°F), heavy snowpack, Shadow Mountain road unplowed.

dangers_and_hazards: Grizzly Bears (Ursus arctos horribilis) and Black Bears active - bear spray mandatory
Steep mountain road inclines and ruts

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional camper or overlander vehicle on Shadow Mountain Road

human_demographics_and_culture: Full-time digital nomads, Grand Teton mountain climbers, overlanders, landscape photographers, and vanlifers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Shoshone and Bannock indigenous traditions revere the Teton peaks ('Teewinot' - Many Pinnacles) and Jackson Hole valley as sacred high-elevation spirit domains.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: World-famous Teton mountain peak energy, high atmospheric ionization, blazing 5G connected solar boondocking.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding aspen forest trail to summit overlook of the entire Teton Range

public_reviews_summary: One of the absolute greatest free boondocking spots on Earth! Unsurpassed 360-degree views of Grand Teton National Park combined with blazing 5G cell internet.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. High solar panel efficiency.

name: Shadow Mountain USFS / BLM Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: US Forest Service - Bridger-Teton National Forest (Jackson Ranger District)

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - USFS / BLM Dispersed Primitive Camping (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed camping at designated pullout sites along Shadow Mountain Loop Road (FR 30340). Strict Forest Service food storage order in effect (grizzly & black bear zone).

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in soil 200 feet from natural springs and drainages. Pack out all toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Pack-In / Pack-Out. Mandatory bear safety disposal.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Dead and down pine firewood collection permitted.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Fully douse with water until cold before leaving.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Summer high wind dry mountain fire restrictions common July-August.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved Dirt / Gravel Mountain Loop Road (FR 30340)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard dirt, steep switchbacks, deep ruts, muddy after rain.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance recommended; standard 2WD vehicles can access lower sites near Antelope Flats Road in dry weather.

nomad_connectivity_rating.overall_rating: Strong / Direct Line of Sight to Jackson Hole Towers
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Unobstructed line of sight across Jackson Hole valley to Teton Range)

amenities: Unrivaled Iconic Grand Teton Range Panorama Views

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 38-55°F, snow melt on mountain loop, crisp sunny mountain air.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 70-84°F, prime mountain camping weather, clear starry nights.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: 42-65°F, golden aspen groves in Jackson Hole, crisp chilly nights.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 10-28°F, deep mountain snowpack, road closed to wheeled vehicles.

dangers_and_hazards: Grizzly and black bear country (certified bear spray & bear canister mandatory)
Steep dirt mountain road ruts when wet

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 9/10 - High mountain breeze and elk bugles in autumn
common_human_made_sounds: Occasional 4x4 vehicle on Shadow Mountain dirt loop

human_demographics_and_culture: Shoshone, Bannock, & Blackfeet ancestral lands, Grand Teton climbers, Jackson Hole digital nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: The Teton peaks (Teewinot - 'Many Pinnacles') carry profound Native American spiritual history as sacred spires of the Creator.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Unrivaled awe-inspiring Teton peak reflections, expansive mountain valley energy, world-class sunsets.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Direct Grand Teton peak overlooks, wildflowers, lodgepole forest

public_reviews_summary: The absolute single best free camping site in the United States. Direct front-row views of Grand Teton National Park, blazing 5G cell internet, and 100% free USFS access.
other_data: Bridger-Teton National Forest. Strict bear food storage order enforced.
